angle: the mark or trace the process leaves behind
subject: A slab of rippled silt lifted out after the water has gone, its cut face showing the cross-laminae each stir-and-settle left, its front ripple profile the one bright line.
controls: settle: shape; the ripples' asymmetry, steep current ripples at 0.1 s (fast drop) easing to round, nearly symmetric ripples at 10 s.
layers: count; one ripple per two partials (crests and cross-lamina sets), 1 to 32 crests, doubling across the range.
stir: shape; ripple height, from a nearly flat bed at 0 to tall ripples at 100 (front profile moves well over 16 px).
grain: shape (planform); the crests go from straight to sinuous, broken linguoid ripples, seeded per crest.
reference: library/toro-blocks (a modelled 3D field projected through one camera, hidden-line)
risks: Three controls change the same ripple field by shape (asymmetry, height, crest planform); they read differently on the slab but share one channel family.
Layers below 4 (2 crests) shows a near-empty slab; at 64 the 32 crests sit around 8 px apart, close to the hatching limit with crest lines plus laminae.
Wave and current ripples are geology; the read is 'ripple marks', not necessarily 'partials', without the motion.
